name: Quickbase
subcategory: spreadsheet databases and operational data apps
tagline: Build a constrained operational database and forms for one small team

pricing.notes: Typical Team monthly seat amount with minimum contract terms.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: 6-month audit-log retention; 14 daily backups plus 6 months of weekly backups; core app building and workflow features.
tiers.notes: Published as an annual-billing starting rate and explicitly excludes an undisclosed platform minimum.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 1-year audit-log retention; SSO and SCIM; sandbox; 14 daily backups plus 6 months of weekly backups.
tiers.notes: Published as an annual-billing starting rate and explicitly excludes an undisclosed platform minimum.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 3-year audit-log retention; custom governance, security, support and capacity.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no permanent free tier; 30-day trial with Business-plan features
pricing.billingTerms: published self-service figures require annual billing; no monthly price is published; every paid plan requires a quote because the platform minimum is excluded
pricing.hiddenCosts: The advertised $35/$55 per-user rates exclude an undisclosed platform minimum; optional Extensions and AI add-ons, implementation services and a separate usage-based licensing model can increase the quote.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Quickbase, build a constrained operational database and forms for one small team. The hard boundary is enterprise governance, integrations, scale, app lifecycle, and support, plus data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Model structured records in a constrained operational database for one small team, provide form, grid, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
whatYouLose: enterprise governance, integrations, scale, app lifecycle, and support
moatNotes: data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations
ongoingBurden: schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Quickbase because teams pay when a flexible database becomes a shared operational system with integrations and years of accumulated business logic. The recurring cost buys schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: NocoDB
priorArt.desc: Active open-source no-code database interface and Airtable alternative.

alternatives.name: Budibase
alternatives.desc: Internal apps, forms, automations, and portals in one box; much closer to Knack than its developer branding suggests.

facts.install: Docker image or Docker Compose; Kubernetes is also supported
facts.engines: Model-agnostic; the agent builder supports bring-your-own AI provider credentials
facts.dataFormat: Built-in app data and app definitions are stored in CouchDB, files in MinIO/S3-compatible object storage, and connected external data remains in its source system
facts.gapVsPaid: It lacks Quickbase's mature cross-app reporting, governance, auditability, and managed operational layer for business-critical team processes.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker and persistent storage; production use also means owning upgrades, TLS, backups, and database/network access

alternatives.name: Corteza
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted business-app suite with records, pages, workflows, charts, and enterprise-grade amounts of configuration.

facts.install: Docker Compose with a configured MySQL or PostgreSQL database
facts.dataFormat: Records and configuration live in the configured SQL database; uploaded attachments live in the server persistence directory
facts.gapVsPaid: Corteza can model records and workflows, but its configuration-heavy self-hosted environment is much less approachable and managed than Quickbase.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker, a database, secrets, persistent-volume permissions, and a reverse proxy/TLS are the first operational hurdle

alternatives.name: Joget Community Edition
alternatives.desc: Forms, lists, workflows, and role-aware apps from a product old enough to have survived several no-code fashions.

facts.install: Download the Community Edition bundle or deploy its Docker image/on-premises package
facts.dataFormat: Application definitions, workflow state, and records live in the configured relational database; uploaded files live on the Joget server
facts.gapVsPaid: It is heavier to administer and less fluid for the spreadsheet-like ad hoc reporting and app changes that Quickbase users expect.
facts.setupBlocker: The first real hurdle is administering a Java web stack and database rather than clicking through a managed signup

alternatives.name: NocoBase
alternatives.desc: Operational records, role-aware pages, forms, charts, and workflows without Quickbase's licensing archaeology.

facts.install: NocoBase CLI or Docker deployment with MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL
facts.engines: Built-in AI employees can connect to common LLMs; exact provider support depends on installed AI plugins
facts.dataFormat: Business data lives in standard relational tables in the configured MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL database; files use configured local or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its younger plugin-driven platform has a smaller integration and governance surface than Quickbase's mature managed operational ecosystem.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a database, secrets, and deployment administration; the community license also preserves NocoBase branding and restricts some uses

alternatives.name: REI3
alternatives.desc: A sober business-app builder with forms, reports, roles, workflows, and no per-user meter.

facts.install: Native Linux/Windows server package or Docker Compose, connected to PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Human-readable application records and configuration live in a PostgreSQL database controlled by the operator
facts.gapVsPaid: REI3 has far fewer ready-made integrations and less mature enterprise governance than Quickbase, so more of the surrounding workflow must be built and operated manually.
facts.setupBlocker: You must provision PostgreSQL and configure a server/reverse proxy; it is not a managed one-click workspace

rejectedAlternatives.name: Saltcorn
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It does the job, but its own security page lists fresh critical RCE, SQL injection, path-traversal, and cross-tenant bugs.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Team plan and a small-team structured database DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Quickbase in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: model structured records in a constrained operational database for one small team, provide form, grid, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create workspaces, bases, tables, fields, records, attachments, relations, and saved views.
Support text, number, currency, date, boolean, select, formula-lite, and relation field types.
Build grid, form, kanban, and record-detail views from one canonical schema.
Add role-based permissions, optimistic concurrency checks, audit history, and trash restore.
Provide CSV import or export and a token-authenticated REST API generated from the schema.
Ship migrations, seed data, backups, health checks, and a schema export format.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out full spreadsheet formula compatibility.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of automations and integrations.
Deliberately leave out large-enterprise governance and vendor-managed scale.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
